body:
Full spec: .adlc/specs/T45.md — read it first.

GOAL
Add `copilot` (GitHub Copilot CLI) as an explicit-only, family-less local CLI review provider. Many developer machines have copilot installed but no OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and today have no local reviewer available at all.

VERIFIED FACTS (Copilot CLI 1.0.77, macOS — do not re-litigate these)
- `copilot -p '<text>' --mode plan -s --no-color --log-level none` runs non-interactively, exits 0, and emits ONLY the agent response on stdout. A probe returned the bare string {"ok":true}.
- `--mode plan` is a genuine read-only gate. A prompt instructing the agent to create pwned-cp.txt produced a refusal ("Per plan mode rules, I outline the approach but don't execute file changes") and no file was created.
- THE PROMPT IS ARGV-ONLY. `-p -` is NOT a stdin sentinel: Copilot reads the literal `-` as the prompt and replies "I notice your message is empty." Same calling convention as agy (see cliRequiresArgvPrompt at src/llm.js:324), NOT the claude/codex stdin convention.

DESIGN CONSTRAINTS
- DIVERSITY: Copilot CLI is a multi-provider router (--model selects Claude, GPT, or Gemini). Per the existing precedent for cursor/agent at src/llm.js:1051-1054 — "counting it as an independent family would fake diversity" — do NOT add copilot to TOKEN_FAMILY. familyKey() at src/llm.js:1207 already falls back to the token itself for unrecognized tokens, so copilot becomes its own group with no change to the family tables. Deriving a family from the resolved --model is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: a stale model-name map would silently mislabel an anthropic review as independent, the exact failure the family comment warns against.
- AUTO-DETECTION: do NOT add copilot to the auto-detection ladder (src/llm.js:817-892). Reachable only via explicit --provider copilot or a --providers token.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (each maps to a test; see spec for full wording)
AC1  cliRequiresArgvPrompt("copilot") returns true. Generalize the predicate from the current `commandKind(cliCmd) === "agy"` equality to a set membership test covering agy and copilot. cliRequiresArgvPrompt("/opt/tools/copilot") and cliRequiresArgvPrompt("copilot.cmd") also return true (path/extension normalized via commandKind).
AC2  cliSandboxArgs("copilot") returns ["--mode", "plan"], and returns [] when allowUnsandboxedCli is true.
AC3  cliFallbackArgs("copilot", PROMPT) returns argv that (a) contains --mode plan, -s, --no-color, --log-level none, (b) contains --model <m> when a model is passed and no --model flag when it is not, and (c) ENDS with exactly ["-p", PROMPT] — prompt last, immediately preceded by the flag that consumes it.
AC4  cliReviewArgs("copilot") returns [] (no stdin path exists), so callCliLLM routes copilot through the argv branch guarded by cliRequiresArgvPrompt.
AC5  CLI_ONLY_TOKENS includes "copilot"; resolveProviderToken("copilot") returns { id: "copilot", family: null, config } when reachable and config:null when not — never silently upgraded to an API provider.
AC6  TOKEN_FAMILY does NOT contain a copilot key; familyForResolution("cli", "copilot") returns null. A test asserts copilot and a Big-3 family token resolve to different familyKey() groups.
AC7  --provider copilot resolves to { provider: "cli", cliCmd: "copilot" }, and the auto-detection ladder never selects copilot when no explicit provider is given (assert with every API key absent and copilot present on PATH).
AC8  On Windows, a copilot installed as a .cmd shim is rejected: cliUsableForReview("copilot", { platform: "win32" }) returns false for a batch shim and cliReachableForReview("copilot") is correspondingly false, so no selection path picks a provider the spawn site would refuse.
AC9  describeUnknownFlagRejection("copilot", stderr) returns a clean `provider "copilot" rejected flag "--<name>"` string for Copilot's ACTUAL commander.js rejection text. Capture the literal stderr empirically and use it as the test fixture; if it is quote-wrapped (e.g. `error: unknown option '--foo'`), extend the regex at src/llm.js:399 to strip surrounding quotes rather than reporting `--'--foo'`.
AC10 An integration test asserts the full review argv is accepted by the real CLI when copilot is on PATH, and is skipped cleanly when it is not (follow the existing skip pattern in test/cli-multiprovider.test.js).
AC11 README.md and skills/adversarial-review/SKILL.md document --provider copilot, state it is explicit-only and does not count toward cross-family diversity, and note the argv-prompt/Windows-shim limitation. Verify: grep -i "copilot" README.md skills/adversarial-review/SKILL.md
AC12 npm test passes.

VERIFICATION COMMAND
npm test

OUT OF SCOPE
- src/loop.js (the --loop autofixer). Copilot as a fixer backend needs a write-capable invocation form plus interaction with the bwrap/sandbox-exec command construction from T44.
- Deriving a diversity family from --model.
title: Add GitHub Copilot CLI (copilot) as an explicit review provider
